Russian philosophical story distinguishes material availability from a work's unfolding relations. Freezing the last note blocks its ending, but recordings and later complete performances are expressly allowed. In the irreversible sculpture case, truthful unrepeatability changes the viewer's situation; the essay expressly leaves its aesthetic value unproved. Future access can justify preservation. Result is accurate description of what was preserved or changed, not a universal duty to destroy or obey an artist's instruction. Aristotle VII–VIII is offered as a limited structural analogy.

Care trial reserves practical public power to end central allocation, while basic assistance remains independently owed. Reporting, reconsideration and practical reservation are distinguished; publicity or temporariness alone do not establish the latter. Affordable transfer capacity constrains implementers under a legitimate adopted mandate, but scarce resources may require revised authorization or a smaller trial. Benefits can properly support continuation; avoidable dependence can separately breach the original limit. The paired mandates locate added value in who may sacrifice flexibility, not discovery of an exit-planning duty. Extensive predecessor overlap, uncertain rights and limits of repair are expressly acknowledged.
